about.title: Sierra Madre Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Sierra Madre is a small foothill community of about 11,163 people in Los Angeles County, and losses here are felt block by block. In the most recent final crash year, 2025, the city logged 14 injury collisions and 17 people hurt, with no traffic deaths recorded. Those numbers are public counts, not a prediction, and wrongful death claims reach well beyond the roadway. A fatal fall at a rental property, a medication error, neglect in a care facility, or a defective product can all give rise to a civil case. Under California law, a spouse or domestic partner and children generally have the first right to bring that case; certain dependents and heirs may qualify when there is no surviving spouse or child. Families usually have two years from the date of death to file, and far less time when a city, county, or state agency is involved. A wrongful death action is separate from any criminal matter, so it can move forward whether or not charges are ever brought. LawProactive connects Sierra Madre families with an independent attorney at no charge, and the attorneys in our network work on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Sierra Madre Families Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits standing in wrongful death cases, giving spouses, domestic partners, and children the first right and then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can confirm where your family stands before anything is filed.

items.title: The deadline is tracked for you
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and claims against a government entity carry a much shorter clock. Your attorney takes ownership of those dates so a grieving family isn't watching a calendar.

items.title: Every recoverable loss is documented
items.desc: Funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance can all be part of a claim. Building that record carefully takes time and experience, and there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My family member died in Sierra Madre but the incident didn't involve a car. Can we still bring a wrongful death claim?
items.answer: Yes. Sierra Madre recorded no traffic deaths in 2025, and many wrongful death cases arise from other causes entirely, such as medical negligence, unsafe property, care-facility neglect, or a faulty product. What matters legally is whether another person or business acted carelessly or wrongfully and that conduct caused the death. An attorney can review the facts and tell you honestly whether a claim exists.

items.question: Is a wrongful death case the same as a criminal prosecution?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action brought by the family, while a criminal case is brought by the prosecutor on behalf of the state. The two proceed independently, and a civil claim can succeed even if no criminal charges are filed. The standard of proof in civil court is also lower than in a criminal trial.

items.question: How long do we have to file in Los Angeles County?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death lawsuit. If a public entity such as the City of Sierra Madre, Los Angeles County, or the State of California may be responsible, a formal government claim usually must be submitted much sooner, often within six months. Because those windows are short and strict, it helps to speak with an attorney as early as you feel able.
